messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx and timeout rates observed for ap-south1 edge pool (edge-ap-south1-pool-17). Metric spike at 13:12 UTC, rolling 5m error rate 18%. Paging on-call (sara_oncall). :rotating_light:

sara_oncall: On it. I can see increased 502/504 and a number of upstream timeouts from the edge proxies. Triage starting — posting summary to exec channel after initial impact.

miguel_sre: I'm grabbing logs from the gateway. Initial look shows large number of outbound NAT connection resets to our egress tier. Suspect NAT gateway saturation / ephemeral port exhaustion.

sara_oncall: Good call. Can we confirm per-pod outbound socket counts?

miguel_sre: Running quick query: ```for pod in $(kubectl get pods -l app=edge-proxy -n prod -o name); do kubectl exec -n prod $pod -- ss -s | head -n 5; done``` Results: several proxies at ~60k ephemeral sockets, close to system limit.

lee_eng_runtime: If NAT is saturated, requests to model workers in other AZs could be getting RSTs. We should shift traffic off ap-south1 edge pool as mitigation and spin up additional edge pool with different egress. Can we reroute at the global LB for a subset of traffic?

sara_oncall: Agreed. Plan: 1) Move critical customer traffic to ap-southeast-1 region (failover policy) for low-latency customers. 2) Reduce incoming concurrency to edge-ap-south1 by lowering connection limit on the gateway for non-critical traffic. 3) Notify support. 4) If NAT cannot be expanded quickly, trigger cross-region steering.

toni_support: I'm composing a status note for affected customers. Which customers are impacted?

sara_oncall: Quick query against routing table shows ~7 enterprise orgs pinned to ap-south1 endpoints. I'll drop a list in a sec.

miguel_sre: I'm attempting ephemeral port bump on the NAT nodes as a short-term fix — increasing net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range and decreasing TIME_WAIT via sysctl. Applying to nodes now. Command: ```sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range='1024 65535' && sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30```

incident-bot: deploy-bot: NAT sysctl change rollout started (canary on 2 nodes).

ash_sales_eng: Heads up — two enterprise customers (acme-inc, starlite) just opened support tickets reporting intermittent 502s. Please include them in updates.

sara_oncall: Noted. @toni_support include ACME and Starlite in initial advisory.

lee_eng_runtime: While MIguel applies sysctl, I'm preparing a targeted routing rule to steer 25% of traffic away from ap-south1 pools to ap-southeast-1. This is a fallback multiplier in the smart router. Command (pseudo): ```redwood route modify --pool edge-ap-south1-pool-17 --steer-away 25% --target edge-ap-southeast-1-pool-02 --reason "NAT saturation"``` Applying in 2m.

miguel_sre: Canary result looks promising — socket usage dropped 30% on the two canary nodes, and 5xx counts decreased ~8% in those pods.

sara_oncall: Okay proceed with staged rollout. Keep canary window 2m between stages and monitor customer errors.

incident-bot: metric-alert: ap-south1 5xx rate down to 12% after canary sysctl, but still above SLO.

toni_support: Draft for customer note: "We are experiencing elevated 5xx in APAC South due to infrastructure egress limits. We're routing critical traffic to nearby region and applying mitigations. Investigating; will update every 15 minutes." Approve?

sara_oncall: Send now. Include contact link + mitigation steps.

miguel_sre: Rolling the routing change to 25% went smooth. 5xx rate for the steered cohort in ap-southeast-1 is ~0.7% — good. Overall ap-south1 global 5xx dropped to 9% after stage 2.

lee_eng_runtime: I'm also enabling a short-term client-side retry-with-backoff policy at the edge for requests hitting generation endpoints — from 3 immediate retries to exponential backoff with jitter. Patch applied at the gateway.

toni_support: Support update sent. Customers thanked us for proactive mitigation. No escalations yet.

sara_oncall: Miguel, can you work with infra to provision additional NAT capacity in ap-south1 as longer-term fix? Estimate on time?

miguel_sre: Request sent to infra team for additional egress NAT instances and to raise ephemeral port table persistently. ETA 40–60 minutes to provision and route.

incident-bot: status-check: first_message_ts=2471357902 current_state=mitigated_partial_failover

ash_sales_eng: Any chance the failover impacted latency-sensitive customers? I'm getting pushback that going to ap-southeast added ~80ms for some endpoints.

sara_oncall: We only steered 25% and prioritized critical traffic to lower-latency links; but yes, some chats may see higher RTT. We're tracking error reduction vs added latency.

lee_eng_runtime: New idea: create a temporary egress pool inside ap-south1 using alternative cloud provider NAT or via a NAT gateway in a neighboring AZ to reduce cross-AZ RSTs. That could shave 20–40ms compared to cross-region. Miguel, can infra attempt?

miguel_sre: Infra working on alternative egress; this is being spun up as I type. Will validate ephemeral port config too.

incident-bot: metric-alert: ap-south1 5xx rate now 6% after routing + sysctl + retries. Customer tickets: 2 open (ACME, Starlite).

sara_oncall: Good progress. I'm going to hand off to miguel_sre for the remainder of the recovery (NAT scaling + postmortem). @miguel_sre you are now the primary on-call for this thread. I'll stay available for comms.

miguel_sre: Ack, taking over. Next steps: complete NAT capacity scale, validate persistent sysctl in node images, monitor for 30m stabilization window, prepare RCA notes.

ton_support: Will continue to update customers every 15m until stable.

lee_eng_runtime: After NAT capacity added, we should reverse the 25% steer gradually. Plan a staggered revert: 10% every 5m with health checks.

miguel_sre: NAT capacity added and validated. Socket headroom restored. Rolling revert now (10% every 3m).

incident-bot: update: last_change=traffic_revert_step_1 new_5xx=3.1%

toni_support: Customers acknowledged the update and appreciate the frequent comms.

sara_oncall: Closing timeline: incident opened 13:12 UTC, mitigations applied 13:16–13:45, handoff 13:48, recovery by 13:54. I'll start a brief blameless postmortem doc in #postmortems and include mitigation timeline and runbook gaps.

miguel_sre: Adding notes: root cause likely ephemeral port exhaustion on NAT nodes under bursty model-worker egress. Action items: persistent sysctl baked into image, autoscale NAT on egress, alert for socket saturation, ROUTE-level graceful failover doc.

incident-bot: incident resolved for now. If errors spike again, reopen thread. :white_check_mark:
